> **What this case shows** — sample entropy scores regularity at one time scale. **Multiscale entropy**
> (Costa 2002) scores it across many, and the *shape* of the curve separates a structured signal from
> noise. This case adds a standalone op (**`multiscaleEntropy`**, completing the entropy family). On a
> real eyes-closed EEG channel it reproduces **NeuroKit2**'s `entropy_multiscale` **bit-for-bit** across
> scales 1–8. And the curve carries a finding: it *rises* to a peak at scale 5, whereas white noise of
> the same size *falls* monotonically — the signature of genuine multi-scale structure in the EEG.

::: {.callout-tip title="The recipe you'll learn"}
**Workflow** — `multiscaleEntropy(x, scales = 1:8)` → the sample entropy at each coarse-grained scale.
**Way of thinking** — read the *shape*, not just the value. A curve that stays high or rises at coarse
scales means structure across time scales; a curve that falls monotonically from scale 1 is what white
noise does. The mean under the curve is a compact complexity index.
**Ecosystem usage** — `PhysioEEG::multiscaleEntropy()`, alongside `sampleEntropy()` and `eegComplexity()`.
:::

## Proposition

On real eyes-closed POz EEG, the new `multiscaleEntropy` reproduces NeuroKit2 `entropy_multiscale` (MSEn)
bit-for-bit across scales 1–8 (max `|diff|` ~4e-16); the curve rises from 1.327 (scale 1) to a peak of
1.879 (scale 5) and stays above scale 1, while a same-size white-noise series falls monotonically.

## Question & goal

**The question is a gap and a shape: the ecosystem had multiscale entropy only inside `eegComplexity` —
can a standalone op reproduce the reference per scale, and does the EEG's curve show the structure that
distinguishes it from noise?** The goal is to introduce `multiscaleEntropy`, certify it per scale, and
read the curve.

## Challenge & approach

At each scale `s`, the signal is coarse-grained into non-overlapping length-`s` window means, and the
sample entropy (`m = 2`, tolerance `r = 0.2·SD` held *fixed on the original* signal) of that series is
the MSE at scale `s`. Matching that convention (fixed tolerance, non-overlapping means) makes the curve
line up with NeuroKit2 exactly. We compute scales 1–8 and compare, and contrast with white noise.

```
EEG POz (eegmmidb) → multiscaleEntropy(scales 1:8) → [1.327, 1.548, 1.595, 1.785, 1.879, 1.762, 1.484, 1.383]
                    vs NeuroKit2 entropy_multiscale (MSEn) → per-scale |diff| ~4e-16 (bit-for-bit)
                    curve RISES to a peak at scale 5   ·   white noise (same N, SD) FALLS monotonically
```

## Data

**EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database (eegmmidb, PhysioNet)**: subject **S002**, run **R02
(eyes-closed)**, channel **POz**, 10 s at 160 Hz — the same git-tracked vector the
[sampen-apen](../sampen-apen-eegmmidb/index.qmd), [svd-entropy](../svd-entropy-eegmmidb/index.qmd) and
[signal-moments](../signal-moments-eegmmidb/index.qmd) cases use. Details in
[`artifacts/data_sources.json`](artifacts/data_sources.json).

## Results

![Left: the multiscale-entropy curve computed by `PhysioEEG::multiscaleEntropy` (filled) and NeuroKit2 `entropy_multiscale` (open circles) — they coincide at every scale (bit-for-bit), peaking at scale 5. Right: the EEG curve rises to a coarse-scale peak, while a white-noise series of the same length and SD falls monotonically — the EEG carries multi-scale structure the noise lacks.](artifacts/figure.png)

*How to read this:* left — the two curves are indistinguishable, the op equals the reference to machine
precision. Right — the crossover tells the story: noise is more irregular at the finest scale but loses
that irregularity under coarse-graining; the EEG *gains* it, because its structure lives at slower scales.

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| MSE at scale 1 (= sample entropy) | 1.327 |
| **MSE peak (scale 5)** | **1.879** |
| MSE at scale 8 | 1.383 |
| mean MSE 1–8 (complexity index) | 1.595 |
| per-scale \|diff\| vs NeuroKit2 | **~4e-16** (bit-for-bit) |
| coarse-scale MSE > scale 1 (structure) | **yes** |

The new op equals NeuroKit2 at every scale, and the rising curve marks multi-scale structure. Values
trace to [`artifacts/mse_summary.csv`](artifacts/mse_summary.csv).

## Conclusion

`multiscaleEntropy` completes the entropy family and is exact against NeuroKit2 at every scale. The
transferable takeaway: **read the MSE curve's shape. A rise or plateau at coarse scales means structure
across time scales; a monotonic fall from scale 1 is the fingerprint of white noise. The eyes-closed EEG
rises — its complexity lives at the slower scales of the alpha rhythm, not just in fast fluctuations.**

## Open questions

- The mean/area under the curve and the peak scale are compact summaries for group comparison, but both
  depend on the maximum scale and the segment length. On a longer recording, extending to scales 1–20 and
  comparing conditions (eyes-open vs eyes-closed, across the scalp) would test whether the coarse-scale
  rise tracks the alpha rhythm. *Documented, not escalated.*

## Using this in your own analysis

| Step | Function | Package |
|---|---|---|
| Multiscale entropy (per scale) | `multiscaleEntropy()` | PhysioEEG |
| Single-scale sample entropy | `sampleEntropy()` | PhysioMoCap |
| Multi-measure complexity wrapper | `eegComplexity()` | PhysioEEG |

**Reading the result.**

- **the curve's shape** — rising/sustained at coarse scales = multi-scale structure; monotonic fall =
  noise-like.
- **the mean (complexity index)** — one number for comparison; pair it with the peak scale.
- **coarse-scale stability** — a coarse-grained series is short (scale `s` leaves `N/s` points), so trust
  high scales only when the segment is long.

**The recipe, copy-runnable:**

```r
library(PhysioEEG)

mse <- multiscaleEntropy(x, scales = 1:8)   # per-scale sample entropy
mean(mse)                                    # complexity index
which.max(mse)                               # peak scale
# the per-scale curve reproduces NeuroKit2 entropy_multiscale bit-for-bit.
```

**Auditing the numbers.** Every value on this page traces to
[`artifacts/mse_summary.csv`](artifacts/mse_summary.csv), and [`audit.py`](audit.py) re-checks the curve,
the bit-exact match against NeuroKit2 at all eight scales, the non-monotonic rise (coarse > fine), and
the honestly noted scope (new standalone op; machine precision; the white-noise structure contrast; the
coarse-scale short-series caveat).
